reading.title: Big events, big costs
reading.text: Hosting a major sporting event such as the Olympics is a dream for many cities. Governments hope the Games will attract tourists and put the city on the map. However, the costs are enormous. New venues are often too large for local needs and stand empty afterwards. To prevent this, recent hosts have broken with convention: Paris 2024 used mostly existing or temporary venues. Economists argue that governments should only intervene with public money if there is a clear plan for what happens after the closing ceremony.

items.q: Why do governments want to host big sporting events?
o: To attract tourists and become better known

items.q: What problem with new venues does the writer mention?
o: They take too long to build.
They are far from the city.

items.q: How did Paris 2024 differ from many earlier hosts?
o: It relied mainly on existing or temporary venues.
